REGULAR MEETING AGENDA CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF CERRITOS AND THE SUCCESSOR AGENCY TO THE CERRITOS REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY THURSDAY - MARCH 8, 2018 - CITY HALL - 07:00 P.M. City Council Chamber AGENDA MATERIALS: Reports and materials related to items on this Agenda are available for public inspection at the City Clerk's Office, Cerritos City Hall, 18125 Bloomfield Avenue, Cerritos, CA 90703, during normal business hours, 8 a.m. to 5 p.m., Monday through Friday, Telephone (562) 916-1248. Materials submitted to the City Council/Successor Agency after distribution of the agenda packet are available for public inspection in the City Clerk's Office at the above address during normal business hours as noted. PUBLIC COMMENTS: For all Agenda Items, except for Consent Calendar Items, public comments will be allowed at the time each matter comes up for discussion. Please complete and submit a blue Speaker's Card to ensure that you are recognized when the Agenda item is considered. The general public comments portion of the meeting, under Agenda Item 6, will not exceed 45 minutes, and no speaker will be allowed more than five minutes, unless determined appropriate by the Chair. To assist in the preparation of appropriate responses, persons are requested, but not required, to state their name and city of residence for the record. PUBLIC HEARINGS: Public hearings will be conducted in the order indicated on the agenda, unless otherwise directed. Please complete and submit a blue Speakers Card if you wish to present testimony. Conduct of public hearings will occur in substantially the following sequence: the item to be heard is announced, a report of written correspondence and staff report are received, and the City Council asks questions of staff. The public hearing is opened and verbal testimony will occur in the following order: the applicant, if applicable, those in favor, opposed, or interested parties, and rebuttal by applicant. Speakers are requested, but not required, to state their name and city of residence for the record. After verbal testimony, the public hearing is closed and the matter is deliberated with a determination being made or a continuation of the matter. 1. Call to Order 2. Invocation The California Court of Appeal has concluded that sectarian prayer as part of the City Council meetings is not permitted under the Constitution. Invocation 3. Comments are limited to 5 minutes per person. 7. Consent Calendar Items under the Consent Calendar are considered routine and will be enacted by one motion. Subject to the discretion of the City Council/Successor Agency, there will be no separate discussion of these items unless a Council/Agency Member or citizen so requests, in which event the item may be removed from the Consent Calendar and considered separately. 7A. Review and consideration of support to lease ALPR technology for two additional Sheriff's patrol vehicles (COUNCIL). Agenda Report 10. Legislative Items 10A. Report on pending legislation. 10B. Review and consideration to support or oppose specific legislation in the State or Federal legislature or in the State or Federal Executive Office for signature. 11. City Council Communications/Committee Reports/Report on Meetings
During this part of the meeting members of the City Council report to the community on various matters of interest, including reports concerning committees on which the Councilmembers serve and reports on meetings/conferences attended. In addition, requests may be made of the staff for reports which will be presented to the City Council at a subsequent meeting, or for the scheduling of future agenda items. There will be no discussion or action taken on any of the items that may be presented during this agenda item. 12. Closed Session 12A. MINUTES OF A REGULAR MEETING OF THE CERRITOS CITY COUNCIL AND THE
SUCCESSOR AGENCY TO THE CERRITOS REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY HELD ON
MARCH 8, 2018, IN THE COUNCIL CHAMBERS AT CERRITOS CITY HALL, 18125
BLOOMFIELD AVENUE, CERRITOS CALIFORNIA

1.  Call to Order

  The meeting was called to order at 7:00 p.m.

2.  Invocation

  The invocation was led by Father John Cordero from Holy Family Catholic
  Church Artesia.

3.  Pledge of Allegiance

  The Pledge of Allegiance was led by Cerritos Girls AYSO All Stars under 12.

4.  Roll Call

  The following members of the City Council/Successor Agency were in attendance:

  Council/Agency Member Jim Edwards
  Council/Agency Member Naresh Solanki
  Council/Agency Member Frank A. Yokoyama
  Mayor Pro Tem/Vice Chair Mark E. Pulido
  Mayor/Chair Grace Hu

5.  Presentations

  None.

6.  Public Comments and Suggestions

  Yanet Lindher spoke regarding the City’s parking permit policy.

  Angel Soto expressed concerns with the implementation of term limits for
  Council members.

  Martin Grossman commented on the Cerritos Center Performing Arts Center
  and the upcoming Mayoral Transition.

  Jane Yen spoke in regard to a statement made by Mayor Pro Tem Pulido at a
  previous meeting and expressed concerns over a robbery at her home, and in
  her neighborhood.

  John Paul Drayer expressed concern with robberies within the City, the future
  of the “Strawberry Patch” property, and commented on Cerritos College Board
  activities.

  C.W. Van der Linden spoke in opposition to any proposed Metro Rail project to
  be built in the City.

  Katherine George Chu expressed concern the handicap-accessible door located
  at Cerritos Park East is not functional.
 City of Cerritos  March 8, 2018
City Council/Successor Agency  Page 2 of 5

6.  Public Comments and Suggestions (continued)

  Sally Havice spoke regarding possible funding cut issues at Cerritos College.

  Daisy Lagasca noted her safety concerns and advised the Council about an
  upcoming PTSA event at Cerritos High School

  Jennifer Pilapil expressed her support for a new City-wide Strategic Plan.

  Crisini Tan expressed concern regarding the parking permit program and
  public safety.

  Murali Vasudevan spoke in regard to Code Enforcement  and  CCPA
  expenditures mentioned at a previous City Council meeting.

7.  Consent Calendar
  Items under the Consent Calendar are considered routine and will be enacted
  by one motion. There will be no separate discussion of these items unless a
  Council/Agency Member or citizen so requests, in which event the item will be
  removed from the Consent Calendar and considered separately.

7A.  Approval of Minutes

  Approval of the City Council/Successor Agency Regular Meeting Minutes of
  February 22, 2018 (COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR AGENCY).
  MOTION: It was moved by Pulido, and seconded by Solanki, to approve the
  City Council/Successor Agency Regular Meeting Minutes of February 22, 2018
  (COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR AGENCY).

  The motion carried (5 – 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Edwards, Solanki, Yokoyama, Pulido, Hu
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

7B.  Approval of Register of Demands

  Approval of the Register of Demands for the City of Cerritos dated March 8,
  2018 (COUNCIL).

  MOTION: It was moved by Pulido, and seconded by Solanki, to approve the
  Register of Demands as follows:

  1. City of Cerritos  2/22/2018  $5,712,843.54  (COUNCIL)

  The motion carried (5 – 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Edwards, Solanki, Yokoyama, Pulido, Hu
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None
 City of Cerritos  March 8, 2018
City Council/Successor Agency  Page 3 of 5

8.  Public Hearings

  None.

9.  New and Old Business

9A.  Award of Bid No. 1324-17 Cerritos Library Radio Frequency Identification
  (RFID) System (COUNCIL).

  A staff report was given by Annie Hylton, City Librarian.

  The Mayor opened public comments. Noting there were no individuals who
  elected to speak, the Mayor closed the public comments.

  MOTION: It was moved by Solanki, and seconded by Edwards, to:

  1. Award Bid No. 1324-17 for the Cerritos Library Radio Frequency
  Identification (RFID) System to Bibliotheca in the amount of $115,885.62
  (COUNCIL).

  The motion carried (5 – 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Edwards, Solanki, Yokoyama, Pulido, Hu
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

9B.  Review and consideration of support to lease ALPR Technology for two
  additional Sheriff’s patrol vehicles (COUNCIL).

  A staff report was given by Daryl Evans, Public Safety Manager. A PowerPoint
  presentation was displayed.

  The Mayor opened public comments.

  Noting there were no individuals who elected to speak, the Mayor closed the
  public comments.

  MOTION: It was moved by Pulido, and seconded by Edwards, to:

  1. Lease two additional ALPR equipped patrol vehicles; and

  2. Authorized the City Manager to increase the Los Angeles County Sheriff’s
  Department’s law enforcement service contract by $9,300 annually to lease
  and deploy two additional ALPR equipped patrol vehicles (COUNCIL).

  The motion carried (5 – 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Edwards, Solanki, Yokoyama, Pulido, Hu
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

10.  Legislative Items

10A.  Report on pending legislation

  None.

10B.  Review and consideration to support or oppose specific legislation in the State
  or Federal legislature or in the State or Federal Executive Office for signature.
  None.
11.  City Council Communications/Committee Reports/Report on Meetings

  Reports were provided by Councilmembers Yokoyama, Mayor Pro Tem Pulido,
  Solanki, and Mayor Hu.

12.  Closed Session

  The City Council recessed to Closed Session to discuss the following items:

12A.  PUBLIC EMPLOYEE PERFORMANCE EVALUATION
  Pursuant to California Government Code Section 54957 (COUNCIL).
  Title: City Manager

12B.  PUBLIC EMPLOYEE PERFORMANCE EVALUATION
  Pursuant to California Government Code Section 54957 (COUNCIL).
  Title: City Attorney

12C.  PUBLIC EMPLOYEE PERFORMANCE EVALUATION
  Pursuant to California Government Code Section 54957 (COUNCIL).
  Title: City Clerk

12D.  CONFERENCE WITH LEGAL COUNSEL – ANTCIPATED LITIGATION (COUNCIL)
  Initiation of litigation pursuant to Government Code Section 54956.9(d)(4) –
  One potential case

  CLOSED SESSION REPORT: The City Council reconvened to Open Session.
  The City Attorney reported the City Council recessed to Closed Session to
  discuss Items 12B and 12D on the Closed Session agenda. Items 12A and 12C
  were not discussed. There was no reportable action taken on Item 12B.

  ITEM 12D MOTION: It was moved by Solanki, and seconded by Hu, to
  authorize the filing of a legal action challenging the Artesia Live II project
  subject to the Artesia City Council approving the project as submitted on
  March 12, 2018.

  The motion carried (5 – 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Edwards, Solanki, Yokoyama, Pulido, Hu
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None
 City of Cerritos  March 8, 2018
City Council/Successor Agency  Page 5 of 5

13.  Adjournment
  The meeting was adjourned at 8:49 p.m. in memory of Ralph Houska.
